questions: Does s-bend progress stay at or above 0.15 with the 12 mm footprint at 1 cm pitch?
Does line_loss_events fall below 1 per run, or stay at 1?
Is max_error still near 0.06 m, and at what progress does each run end?
Does rms_error stay near 0.03 on all tracks? If so, the offset is probably a motor-mismatch term, which is a controller question.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line losses stay at 1 with progress unchanged, tell me whether the line_loss setting (last_direction versus search) would help more than further geometry. If progress falls below 0.11 on the oval, restore sensor_size 0.016 m.

intent: Single-variable test from iteration 6: keep the seven-sensor, 1 cm pitch, 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track layout, and change only sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m. This tests whether heavy overlap between neighbouring 16 mm footprints is blurring the signal. Expect s-bend progress at or above 0.15, oval at or above 0.11, and line_loss_events at or below 1 per run. Weights for the Integrator: x/0.015, giving -2, -1.333, -0.667, 0, 0.667, 1.333, 2.
learning: Iteration 6 (7 sensors, 16 mm, 1 cm pitch, 4 cm lead) gave s-bend 0.155, oval 0.11, slalom 0.1075, and one line loss per run. Pitch of 1 cm or 1.5 cm is safe, and pitch of 2 cm or wider collapses s-bend progress. Footprint is neutral at 1.5 cm pitch (iterations 1 and 4). Next I measure footprint at 1 cm pitch. Remaining losses (one per run, max_error about 0.06 m) point to controller or line_loss handling rather than span or lead, since no geometry tested so far has removed them.
rationale: Iteration 6 (seven 16 mm sensors at 1 cm pitch, x = -0.03 to +0.03, 4 cm lead) restored s-bend progress to 0.155, matching the iteration 4 reference. Its score was 51.11, level with iterations 1 and 4. The 2 cm pitch is therefore the cause of the s-bend collapse in iterations 2, 3 and 5, not the 4 cm lead, and the 1 cm pitch is kept. The design now plateaus near 51 with one line loss per run and max_error about 0.06 to 0.068 m, so the remaining limit is not pitch or lead. Iteration 0 (1 cm pitch, 12 mm footprints, 2 cm span) also avoided the collapse, but it used a narrower span. Iteration 4 showed that 16 mm versus 12 mm footprints made no measurable difference at 1.5 cm pitch. The one geometry variable not yet tested at the good layout is footprint at 1 cm pitch. Seven sensors at 1 cm pitch overlap heavily, so the 16 mm footprint may over-weight the outer sensors and blur the signal. I therefore change only sensor_size, from 16 mm to 12 mm, and keep the iteration 6 layout. The weights for the Integrator are x/0.015, which matches the iteration 4 slope. Expected result: s-bend progress at or above 0.15 and one or fewer line losses per run, with score at or above about 51. If progress falls below 0.11, the 16 mm footprint was needed, and the next lever is the Integrator's line_loss setting or gains, not geometry.
